clinics.name: Oasis of Hope Hospital
specialties: Dendritic cell and NK cell therapies
clinics.namedDoctors: Dr. Francisco Contreras (Director, President and Chairman; described on the site as an oncologist and surgeon), Dr. Francisco Cecena (Director of Oncology), Dra. Paulina Larraga (Medical Director), Dr. Carlos Gutierrez (Admissions Physician), Dra. Samantha Ramos (Attending Physician). No board certification, cédula or society membership is shown for any of them on the site. No anesthesiologist is named. Treatment takes place in the clinic's own hospital building at Paseo Playas de Tijuana 19; whether that building is CSG-certified could not be confirmed (see credentials).
clinics.credentials: CSG: Not on the CSG certified list (checked October 30, 2026 against the Consejo de Salubridad General 'Establecimientos de Atención Médica con Certificado Vigente' PDF consolidated to September 1, 2026, which lists 15 establishments nationwide and none in Baja California or Sonora; the earlier list of May 2, 2024 with 86 establishments carried only Hospital Velmar, Ensenada, expiring December 2, 2025, and PRO-MED Grupo Médico, Mexicali, expiring April 28, 2025, for Baja California); no third-party source claims CSG certification for Oasis of Hope. COFEPRIS: no licencia sanitaria number is published on the site; no COFEPRIS alert naming the hospital was found in a search on October 30, 2026. JCI: the Joint Commission directory returned HTTP 403 to automated reading on October 30, 2026; the site does not claim JCI. No accreditation of any kind is named on the site. Founded 1963 by Ernesto Contreras (site and Wikipedia). SEP cédula lookup: not checked (interactive form).
clinics.cautions: The hospital's cell therapies (dendritic cell, LAK, tumor lysate, TIL, NK cell) and its metabolic programme are not FDA-approved cancer treatments and the site displays no regulatory disclaimer; it instead publishes stage IV survival percentages against a 'national average' without methodology, patient numbers or time frame (oasis-site). Wikipedia, citing The Guardian, Cancer Research UK, Memorial Sloan Kettering and Quackwatch, records that the founder was placed on the American Cancer Society's 'unproven methods' list in 1971, that Memorial Sloan Kettering lists 'Contreras Therapy' among regimens that 'show no evidence of efficacy', that the hospital historically used laetrile/amygdalin, which a Cochrane review associates with cyanide poisoning, and that Cancer Research UK's Richard Sullivan said 'the Tijuana clinics are essentially set up to deceive' (oasis-wikipedia). In the UK, Nottingham Trading Standards instructed the affiliated Oasis of Hope UK office to remove cancer claims from its website under the Cancer Act 1939 (oasis-goodthinking). No deaths, lawsuits, CDC/FDA notices or COFEPRIS suspensions naming the Tijuana hospital were found in press searches on October 30, 2026. Patient fundraising pages describe treatment estimates of about $56,000 with $29,000 required up front, and follow-up weeks budgeted at about $10,000; these are individual patient budgets, not published rates (oasis-gofundme).
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site. The admissions page promises 'A transparent estimate of treatment costs' after a free consultation. Indicative only: patient GoFundMe pages (2020s, undated) cite a $56,000 total with $29,000 up front, and $10,000 per follow-up week.

booking.channels: Phone +1 (619) 690-8450 (a toll-free (888) 500-4673 appears only in page metadata); contact form https://www.oasisofhope.com/contact-us/; address Paseo Playas de Tijuana 19, Fracc. Playas de Tijuana. No email or WhatsApp published. Hours not published.
booking.consult: Free 45-minute Zoom consultation, then submit medical records (CMP, CBC, urinalysis, CT/MRI/PET reports, pathology report, tumor markers, oncology notes) and a Medical Questionnaire; the medical team returns a treatment recommendation and a cost estimate. Deposit terms and response time are not published.
booking.languages: English and Spanish (site in English; Tijuana facility).

clinics.name: Hospital CER / CER Bariatrics (Dr. José Alberto Carlos Rivas)
clinics.namedDoctors: Dr. José Alberto Carlos Rivas ('Dr. Alberto Carlos'): the CER Bariatrics page states he is certified by the Consejo Mexicano de Cirugía General (2012), board-certified in bariatric surgery by the Colegio Mexicano de Cirugía para la Obesidad y Enfermedades Metabólicas (CMCOEM), and a Fellow of the American College of Surgeons (2020), with a link to facs.org/profile/56114824; medical degree Universidad Autónoma de Nayarit 2006, general surgery residency IMSS Centro Médico Nacional del Noroeste 2008 to 2012. No cédula number is shown. Dr. Luis Suárez is listed by name only. Plastic surgeons are not named on the CER Plastic Surgery page (patients' reviews mention Dr. Eduardo Ochoa, Dr. Elsy and Dr. Montufar). No anesthesiologist is named on either site. Surgery takes place inside Hospital CER, Av. Diego Rivera 2386, Zona Río, which the operator describes as a surgical-specialty hospital rather than a general hospital. CSG status of Hospital CER: not confirmed (see credentials).
clinics.credentials: CSG: Not on the CSG certified list (checked October 30, 2026 against the Consejo de Salubridad General 'Establecimientos de Atención Médica con Certificado Vigente' PDF consolidated to September 1, 2026, which lists 15 establishments nationwide and none in Baja California or Sonora; the earlier list of May 2, 2024 with 86 establishments carried only Hospital Velmar, Ensenada, expiring December 2, 2025, and PRO-MED Grupo Médico, Mexicali, expiring April 28, 2025, for Baja California); no source claims CSG certification for Hospital CER. COFEPRIS: no licencia sanitaria number is shown on cerbariatrics.com or cerplasticsurgery.com; no COFEPRIS alert naming CER was found (search October 30, 2026). The hospital's own site cerhospital.com returned HTTP 503 and then 406 to automated reading on October 30, 2026; facts come from the CER Bariatrics and CER Plastic Surgery brand sites and third-party listings. One directory gives 100 beds and 85 doctors but is inconsistent with other listings; ICU capacity is not stated anywhere seen. Hospital established 2008 per a third-party profile (not confirmed on an official page). JCI: not claimed. CMCPER directory: blocked by a Cloudflare challenge on October 30, 2026, so plastic surgeon board status is unverified.
clinics.cautions: Structural: both consumer-facing brands are marketing entities. The CER Plastic Surgery footer states 'we are not a medical provider, and as such, we do not offer medical services or treatment', and CER Bariatrics says it provides 'access to' certified surgeons (cer-plastic-site, cer-bariatrics-site). Plastic surgeons are not named on the plastic surgery site, and no anesthesiologist is named on either brand site. The hospital is described as dedicated to surgical specialties, so ICU and emergency depth could not be confirmed. No deaths, lawsuits or COFEPRIS suspensions naming Hospital CER were found in English or Spanish press searches on October 30, 2026.
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site. Both brand sites say 'Request a quote' or 'Get Your Free Quote' and advertise savings 'up to 70%' without listing prices. Marketplace range (indicative): Tijuana all-inclusive gastric sleeve packages at other providers are listed at roughly $4,000 to $5,500 in 2025 to 2026 aggregator pages.

booking.channels: CER Bariatrics: online case form 'Start My Free Evaluation' at https://www.cerbariatrics.com/ (no phone, email or WhatsApp on the page); patient portal; Facebook support group. CER Plastic Surgery: phone +1 619-841-9001, virtual consultation form at https://www.cerplasticsurgery.com/, email obscured on page. Hospital address Av. Diego Rivera 2386, Zona Río, Tijuana.
booking.consult: Submit a case online for review; 'Submitting your case does not commit you to surgery.' Quote and inclusions are confirmed with a coordinator. Fee, response time and deposit terms are not published. Financing offered subject to third-party approval.

clinics.name: Mexico Bariatric Center (SOURCiS, Inc., facilitator; surgery at Hospital Azar)
clinics.district: Tijuana (Aviación, Blvd. Salinas; US office Folsom, California)
clinics.namedDoctors: Bariatric: Dr. Alejandro Gutiérrez ('Chief Bariatric Surgeon'), Dr. Miguel Montalvo, Dr. Jacqui Osuna, Dr. Jesús Ceja, plus Dr. Zapata, Dr. Fredy and Dr. Azucena listed by surname or first name only. The site describes the network as 'Double Board-Certified in Bariatrics (CMCOEM)' with FACS and IFSO membership but attaches no certificate or cédula number to any individual. No anesthesiologist is named. Surgery is performed at Hospital Azar, Blvd. Salinas 11050, Aviación, Tijuana, which the site says 'officially opened its doors in 2024'; the cost page lists 'Accredited Hospital with ICU' without naming the accreditor. CSG status of Hospital Azar: not confirmed.
clinics.credentials: Operator: SOURCiS, Inc. DBA Mexico Bariatric Center, 193 Blue Ravine Rd Ste 140, Folsom, CA 95630; the legal disclaimer states it 'is a medical tourism facilitator, and not a healthcare provider'. CSG: Not on the CSG certified list (checked October 30, 2026 against the Consejo de Salubridad General 'Establecimientos de Atención Médica con Certificado Vigente' PDF consolidated to September 1, 2026, which lists 15 establishments nationwide and none in Baja California or Sonora; the earlier list of May 2, 2024 with 86 establishments carried only Hospital Velmar, Ensenada, expiring December 2, 2025, and PRO-MED Grupo Médico, Mexicali, expiring April 28, 2025, for Baja California); no source names a CSG certificate for Hospital Azar. COFEPRIS: no licencia sanitaria number shown; no COFEPRIS alert naming the brand or Hospital Azar found (search October 30, 2026). Site claims an A+ BBB rating, Medical Tourism Association certification and HONcode compliance (claims not verified against the issuers). JCI: not claimed. SEP cédula: not checked.
clinics.cautions: Structural: broker-run brand with a rotating roster of surgeons and a hospital that opened in 2024; the facilitator disclaims provider status, so clinical responsibility sits with the Mexican surgeon and hospital. The site publishes a '99.3% safety rate' and '30,606 lives transformed' as self-reported figures without methodology (mbc-site). A consumer-complaint site hosts reviews of SOURCiS alleging a refund offer conditioned on a non-disclosure agreement barring negative reviews and BBB complaints, and a duodenal switch complicated by vein damage and bleeding; these are unverified self-reported accounts from around 2022 (mbc-complaintsboard). No deaths, lawsuits or regulator actions naming Mexico Bariatric Center or Hospital Azar were found in press searches on October 30, 2026. Price exclusions: airfare, higher BMI (about 49 and above), hiatal hernia repair and prior abdominal surgery carry extra charges.
clinics.publishedPrices: Published on its site (USD): gastric sleeve 'starting at $4,495*', footnote 'Prices are subject to change. Not valid on blackout dates', page marked 'Last Updated: 2025' with a post timestamp of September 16, 2026 (mbc-cost). Deposit $395 after health-questionnaire approval (mbc-site). The 'Our Costs and Packages' and deposit-policy pages returned 404 on October 30, 2026.

booking.channels: US toll-free 855-768-7247; Tijuana +52 664 905 3362; US fax 1-855-453-2329; online Health Questionnaire, 'Book Your Surgery' and 'Make a Payment' forms at https://www.mexicobariatriccenter.com/. No email or WhatsApp published.

booking.languages: English and Spanish; US-based coordinators and a US surgeon liaison.
booking.includes: Private ground transport from San Diego, hospital with ICU, 2 nights in a 4.5-star hotel, discounted complication coverage, FMLA forms, nutrition programme, online support group. Excludes airfare, high-BMI and hiatal hernia surcharges.

clinics.credentials: The site claims Joint Commission International accreditation 'three times', Global Healthcare Accreditation, 'Quality Management Solutions' and 'International Center of Excellence'. JCI: the Joint Commission directory returned HTTP 403 to automated reading on October 30, 2026, so the claim is unverified against the accreditor. CSG: Not on the CSG certified list (checked October 30, 2026 against the Consejo de Salubridad General 'Establecimientos de Atención Médica con Certificado Vigente' PDF consolidated to September 1, 2026, which lists 15 establishments nationwide and none in Baja California or Sonora; the earlier list of May 2, 2024 with 86 establishments carried only Hospital Velmar, Ensenada, expiring December 2, 2025, and PRO-MED Grupo Médico, Mexicali, expiring April 28, 2025, for Baja California). COFEPRIS: the footer shows 'Permiso de Publicidad Número 233300201A0601' (an advertising permit, not a licencia sanitaria) and Dr. Ortiz's cédula 3181627; no licencia sanitaria number is shown and no COFEPRIS alert naming OCC was found (search October 30, 2026). The same reporting says only Hospital Arcángeles (a different facility) was suspended. No later outcome of the Breen investigation was found in press searches on October 30, 2026. Structural: the consumer brand describes itself as a scheduling facilitator, not a healthcare provider, and the surgeons' Mexican-only licensure is stated on the site (occ-site).

clinics.cautions: The site's 'only certified hospital in Ensenada' claim is not supported by the current CSG list; the certificate on the 2024 list expired December 2, 2025 and no renewal appears as of September 1, 2026 (csg-list, csg-list-2024). Bariatric packages are sold through brokers rather than the hospital site. No deaths, lawsuits or COEPRIS suspensions naming Hospital Velmar were found in English or Spanish press searches on October 30, 2026.
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site apart from an annual membership of MXN 1,500 plus IVA (about $80 at MXN 18.7 = $1). Marketplace range (indicative): PlacidWay broker packages list a gastric bypass at Hospital Velmar from $9,699 and a sleeve from $6,899 (undated).
